title: 1977 AHSME Problem 4
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) \(AB=AC\) and \(\angle A=80^\circ.\) If points \(D,\) \(E\) and \(F\) lie on sides \(BC,\) \(AC\) and \(AB,\) respectively, and \(CE=CD\) and \(BF=BD,\) then \(\angle EDF\) equals

solutions.text:
The base angles of \(\triangle ABC\) are each \(50^\circ.\) Since \(CE=CD,\) triangle \(CED\) has vertex angle \(50^\circ,\) so \(\angle EDC=65^\circ.\) Similarly, \(BF=BD\) gives \(\angle BDF=65^\circ.\) The three angles above the straight line \(CB\) sum to \(180^\circ,\) so \[ \begin{aligned} \angle EDF&=180^\circ-65^\circ-65^\circ\\ &=50^\circ. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is C.

Use the two given equal-length pairs to find \(\angle EDC\) and \(\angle BDF\)
